question.text: Will FURA introduce another cultivated meat dish on its menu before July 2027?
question.resolution_criteria: This question will resolve as **Yes** if at any time before July 1, 2027, FURA has at least one item on its menu that contains a cultured meat other than Japanese quail.

research:
Going by FURA's own menu page, the question has not resolved: the only cultured meat listed is Japanese quail, and I found no sign of FURA adding a second species.

## 1. Resolution source
- 2026-11-12 (fetched today, the page shows no date): FURA's menu lists two items with cultured meat, and both use quail. One is the snack "A Quail Walks Into a Bar" (Forged parfait, cultured Japanese quail). The other is the cocktail "A Quail Walks Into a Martini". "Bread & Butter (ish)" uses Forged tallow, which earlier coverage says is a byproduct of the same quail. The jellyfish and insect items are not described as cultured. No other cultured meat appears (no chicken, duck, beef or pork). [fura.space/menu](https://www.fura.space/menu)

## 2. Current status
- The question is not settled. All cultured meat on the menu is Japanese quail, which does not count.
- I could not find anything linking FURA to Parima, Good Meat, Aleph or any other cultured meat supplier.
- Vow's second product, Forged Gras, is also made from Japanese quail, so it would not count if FURA added it. [Robb Report SG](https://robbreport.com.sg/forged-gras-vow/), [FoodBev](https://www.foodbev.com/post301/vow-launches-cultured-quail-foie-gras-becomes-first-company-to-sell-multiple-cultured-meat-produc)

## 3. Recent news (newest first)
- 2026-09 (approximate): A Corner listing calls FURA a future-food gastrobar serving "bugs, lab-grown meats and cocktails". It does not name any new product. [Corner](https://www.corner.inc/place/pFHMXxcB2zey)
- 2026-08-04: Singapore approved Aleph Farms' Cultivated Thin-Cut Steak, which mixes cultivated beef cells with plant protein. Aleph expects its Singapore production line to start in the first half of 2027, launching "with select restaurant partners" first. [FoodNavigator](https://www.foodnavigator.com/Article/2026/08/04/cultivated-beef-steak-to-hit-singapore-food-scene-with-historic-approval/), [Green Queen](https://www.greenqueen.com.hk/aleph-farms-lab-grown-meat-cultivated-beef-singapore-approval-launch/), [Just Food](https://www.just-food.com/news/aleph-farms-to-launch-cultivated-steak-in-singapore-next-year-after-gaining-regulatory-approval/)
- 2026-04: Singapore cleared Parima's cultivated duck, after its chicken was cleared in October 2025. Parima plans to sell the duck through high-end restaurants in Singapore, under its culinary brand Gourmey. [Food Ingredients First](https://www.foodingredientsfirst.com/news/parima-secures-regulatory-clearance-to-sell-cultivated-duck-in-singapore.html), [Food Business MEA](https://www.foodbusinessmea.com/parima-secures-second-cultivated-meat-approval-in-singapore-for-duck-product/), [vegconomist](https://vegconomist.com/category/cultivated-cell-cultured-biotechnology/approvals/)
- 2026-04-11: A Star feature says FURA is "heavily invested" in future ingredients, including cultivated proteins, and names only the cultivated quail. It mentions no plans for new cultivated products. [The Star](https://www.thestar.com.my/lifestyle/living/2026/04/11/singapore-restaurants-bricolage-and-fura-are-building-the-menus-of-the-future)
- 2025-03: FURA launched Journal of Future Foods Volume Two. I found no coverage of a Volume Three. [The Spirits Business](https://www.thespiritsbusiness.com/2025/03/fura-unveils-new-menu/), [Jigger Daily](https://jiggerdaily.com/fura-singapore-cocktail-menu-journal-of-future-foods-volume-two/)
- 2025-08-14: Vow said it had served more than 25,000 dishes since April 2024, and named FURA's quail candle and cocktail as examples of its products in use. [FoodNavigator Asia](https://www.foodnavigator-asia.com/Article/2025/08/14/vow-eyes-apac-growth-with-cultured-quail/)
- The news articles you supplied (Green Queen Quick Bites, Meatly and others) say nothing about FURA or cultured meat in Singapore restaurants. I checked the Green Queen piece directly.

## 4. Base rates
- FURA opened in late 2023. In roughly three years it has served only one cultured species, Vow's quail, which Singapore approved in April 2024. It added the quail in several forms (parfait, martini, tallow candle) rather than adding new species.
- It has released menu volumes about every 1 to 1.5 years (Volume One around late 2023, Volume Two in March 2025). That timing points to a possible Volume Three around now or in the first half of 2027, but I have not confirmed one.
- Supply has grown: Singapore now has approved cultured products from Good Meat (chicken), Vow (quail), Parima (chicken and duck) and Aleph (beef). The only cultured chicken service I found in my searches is Good Meat's Thursday-night chicken at Huber's Butchery. [Cultivated X](https://cultivated-x.com/approvals/cultivated-meat-2026-close-dozen-approvals-none-yet-selling-at-scale/), [Green Queen](https://www.greenqueen.com.hk/fura-singapore-journal-of-future-food-menu-asias-50-best-bars/)

## 5. Other forecasts
- I found no Polymarket, Kalshi, Manifold or Metaculus market on this question or anything close to it. None of the Kalshi markets supplied with the question (quahog landings, broiler production, the FAO index, menu prices, Starship) are relevant.

## 6. Upcoming events before resolution
- First half of 2027: Aleph's Singapore production is due to start, with restaurant partners first. That makes FURA a plausible but unconfirmed early partner. Aleph's launches have slipped before.
- Parima/Gourmey's duck is aimed at high-end Singapore restaurants. No launch partners have been announced.
- A possible new FURA menu (Volume Three) is the most likely moment for a new dish to be added.
- Vow is also a risk on the supply side. I found no dated 2026 news on its Singapore operations, so any change to Vow's supply could change FURA's mix of future-protein dishes.

Gaps: I could not see FURA's Instagram or other social channels, and found no 2026 interviews with its founders about new cultivated proteins.

### 1. Resolution source
- 2026-11-12 (fetched today, the page shows no date): the resolution source, [fura.space/menu](https://www.fura.space/menu), lists exactly one cultured meat, Japanese quail. It appears in two places:

  - "A Quail Walks Into a Martini".
- Same page: "Bread & Butter (ish)" uses "Forged tallow", which is a byproduct of Vow's quail process, so it is not a new species. The page marks items with "(FP)" for "future protein" but doesn't define the term. The other FP items are Jellyfish Ceviche (wild jellyfish) and Pumpkin Layers (cricket garum), neither of them cultured meat. There is no chicken, pork, beef, duck or foie gras. [FURA menu](https://www.fura.space/menu)

### 2. Current status
- 2026-11-12: nothing has resolved the question. The menu is unchanged from the question background (April 2026): quail is the only cultured meat. I found no announcement from FURA or a supplier about a second cultured protein.

### 3. Recent news (newest first)

- 2026-04-15/16: SFA authorised Parima's cultivated duck, sold under the Gourmey brand. This followed approval of its cultivated chicken in October 2025. Parima plans to launch "through premium culinary channels" in Singapore, including foie-gras-style uses. I found no restaurant partners or launch date. [FoodNavigator](https://www.foodnavigator.com/Article/2026/04/15/parima-gets-regulatory-approval-for-cultivated-foie-gras/), [Gourmey](https://gourmey.com/blogs/parima-becomes-the-first-european-company-to-obtain-approval-for-cultivated-meat)
- 2026-04-11: a Star feature describes FURA's cultivated quail and calls it one of the first restaurants in Southeast Asia to use cultivated proteins. It mentions no plans for new cultured products. [The Star](https://www.thestar.com.my/lifestyle/living/2026/04/11/singapore-restaurants-bricolage-and-fura-are-building-the-menus-of-the-future)
- 2025-05-05: a Green Queen profile of the Volume Two menu covers only Vow's quail. Co-owner Christina Rasmussen says the aim is "a glimpse of what our diet could look like in the future", but names no upcoming additions. [Green Queen](https://www.greenqueen.com.hk/fura-singapore-journal-of-future-food-menu-asias-50-best-bars/)
- Around March 2025: "Journal of Future Foods, Volume Two" launched with the quail martini and parfait. [The Spirits Business](https://www.thespiritsbusiness.com/2025/03/fura-unveils-new-menu/), [Jigger Daily](https://jiggerdaily.com/fura-singapore-cocktail-menu-journal-of-future-foods-volume-two/)

### 4. Base rates
- FURA opened in October 2023 and has been running for about 3 years. In that time it has used one cultured meat species, Vow's quail, which Singapore approved in April 2024. It has not added a second species, even though Singapore had approved GOOD Meat chicken since 2020 and Parima chicken since October 2025. [Vow/FURA feed](https://www.forgedbyvow.com/the-feed/forged-by-fura), [FoodNavigator regulation overview](https://www.foodnavigator.com/Article/2026/02/18/cultivated-meat-regulation-where-countries-stand-in-2026/)
- FURA's major menu volumes seem to come out roughly once every 1 to 1.5 years. Volume Two launched around March 2025, and I found no Volume Three by November 2026, so a new volume may be due.
- Approved cultivated products in Singapore so far: GOOD Meat chicken, Vow quail, Parima chicken and duck, Aleph beef, which makes five or more. Reaching restaurants is usually slow and limited, with small volumes. One analysis notes that Aleph is "cleared to sell... and is selling in neither" market. [Lifematetech](https://lifematetech.com/articles/aleph-farms-two-approvals-no-production-line)

### 5. Other forecasts
- I found no Polymarket, Kalshi, Manifold or Metaculus market on this or a closely related question. None of the Kalshi markets supplied with the brief (quahog landings, broiler production, FAO food price index, fast food prices, Starship) is relevant.

### 6. Upcoming events before resolution
- First half of 2027: Aleph Farms plans to start its Singapore production line and launch with select restaurants. FURA is a plausible partner but has not been named. [Green Queen](https://www.greenqueen.com.hk/aleph-farms-lab-grown-meat-cultivated-beef-singapore-approval-launch/)
- Date unknown: Parima/Gourmey's premium foodservice rollout of duck and chicken in Singapore.
- Possibly late 2026 or 2027: FURA's next "Journal of Future Foods" volume. I found no announcement.
- Possibly 2026-2027: new species from Vow. I found nothing in 2026 beyond its Japanese quail products.
- Asia's 50 Best Bars (usually spring) and the Spirited Awards (July 2027, after the deadline) are typical occasions for menu launches and publicity.

Gaps: I could not find any statement from FURA about plans for cultured proteins other than quail, and no restaurant partners have been named for the Aleph or Parima launches.

forecasts.reasoning:
(a) About 7.5 months remain (to July 1, 2027). Yes requires FURA's menu to list, at any point before then, at least one item containing a cultured meat other than Japanese quail, such as Parima/Gourmey chicken or duck, Aleph beef or GOOD Meat chicken. Vow's Forged Gras is also Japanese quail, so it would not count.

(b) Status quo: as of 2026-11-12, all the cultured meat on FURA's menu is Japanese quail (parfait, martini and tallow). If nothing changes, the answer is No.

(c) Base rate: FURA has had about 36 months of operation with zero second species added. That is despite GOOD Meat chicken being approved since 2020 and Parima chicken since October 2025. On a naive per-month hazard this suggests well under 10% for a 7.5-month window. However, the supply environment has changed: Parima duck was approved in April 2026 and Aleph beef in August 2026. Restaurants like FURA are the typical first channel for new products. Adjusting for that, a reference-class rate of roughly 10-15% fits.

(d) Evidence:
- For Yes:
  - Aleph's approval (2026-08-04) targets launch with select restaurant partners in the first half of 2027, and talks are "active."
  - Parima's duck approval (April 2026) targets premium Singapore culinary channels.
  - FURA was named World's Best Bar on 2026-07-23, which makes it the most obvious showcase venue for future proteins.
  - A Volume Three menu may be due, since Volume Two launched in March 2025.
- For No:
  - FURA has shown no move toward a second species in three years.
  - No partner announcements from FURA, Aleph or Parima.
  - Aleph's history includes slipped timelines, and one analysis notes it is "selling in neither" approved market.
  - FURA has deepened its use of the quail rather than broadening to other species.
  - Coverage on 2026-04-11 mentioned no plans for new cultured products.

(e) No scenario: Aleph's line slips past mid-2027 or launches with other restaurants. Parima rolls out slowly through fine-dining chefs, and FURA's next menu reworks the quail and insects. Yes scenario: Aleph or Parima picks FURA as a launch partner for publicity, and a Volume Three menu or limited special in spring 2027 lists cultivated duck or beef on the website.

(f) I start at about 12%. I add a few points for the newly available supply and FURA's profile, and because brief specials also count. Short timelines and the lack of any signal keep this low. My final estimate is about 15%.

Probability: 15%

(a) About 7.5 months remain, until July 1, 2027. For Yes, FURA's menu must list, at some point before that date, at least one item containing a cultured meat other than Japanese quail, for example Parima's chicken or duck, Aleph's beef, GOOD Meat's chicken, or a new Vow species.

(b) If nothing changes, the answer is No. As of 2026-11-12 the menu lists only Vow's cultured Japanese quail, in the parfait, the martini and the tallow butter.

(c) Base rate: FURA has been open for about 3 years and has had quail for about 2.5 years. In that time it never added a second species, even though GOOD Meat chicken has been approved since 2020 and Parima chicken since October 2025. The reference class is niche restaurants adding a newly approved cultivated protein within a given 7-month window. Cultivated meat rollouts are slow and small, so this happens rarely, perhaps 10% of the time.

(d) Evidence:
- For Yes:
  - Singapore approved Aleph Farms' beef on 2026-08-04, with a restaurant-partner launch targeted for the first half of 2027 and "active" talks with restaurants.
  - Singapore approved Parima's duck in April 2026, aimed at premium culinary channels.
  - FURA won World's Best Bar in July 2026, which makes it a strong showcase partner for suppliers.
  - FURA's menu volume cycle (Volume Two came in March 2025) suggests a Volume Three may be due.
- For No:
  - FURA has added no second species in about 2.5 years despite available supply.
  - The 2026-04-11 Star feature mentions only quail.
  - No partners have been named for Aleph or Parima.
  - Aleph's launches have historically slipped, and its "approved but selling nowhere" pattern continues.
  - Volume Three is unconfirmed.

(e) Scenarios:
- No: Aleph's production line slips past mid-2027. Parima launches with a fine-dining restaurant, not FURA. FURA's next menu deepens its use of quail plus insects and plant-based items.
- Yes: FURA's Volume Three launches in spring 2027 with a Parima cultivated duck dish or an Aleph steak bite as a launch-partner showcase, and it appears on the website menu.

(f) I start from about 10% and move up modestly. Two new suppliers are actively seeking restaurant partners in Singapore within the window, and FURA is arguably the city's most natural venue for showcasing future food. Against that, timelines tend to slip, FURA has a record of staying with one species, and the window is short. I land at about 14%.

Probability: 14%

(a) There are about 7.5 months left, from 2026-11-12 to 2027-07-01. For Yes, FURA's menu must at some point list an item containing a cultured meat other than Japanese quail, such as Parima chicken or duck, Aleph beef or GOOD Meat chicken. Vow's Forged Gras would not count, because it is also made from quail.

(b) If nothing changes, the answer is No. On 2026-11-12 the menu lists only cultured quail, as a parfait, a martini and tallow.

(c) Base rate: FURA has offered one cultured species for about 2.5 years. GOOD Meat chicken has been available since 2020 and Parima chicken since October 2025, and FURA added neither. Treating each 7 to 8 month window as one trial gives roughly 0 successes in 3 to 4 windows. Restaurants adopting a newly approved cultured product within a few months is also rare, because production volumes are small. That puts the base rate at about 10%.

(d) Evidence for Yes:
- Singapore approved Parima duck in April 2026, aimed at premium restaurants, and it suits foie-gras-style use, which matches FURA's parfait concept.
- Aleph beef was approved on 2026-08-04, with a launch through "select restaurant partners" planned for H1 2027.
- FURA was named World's Best Bar in July 2026, which makes it an ideal showcase partner.
- A Volume Three menu looks due, since Volume Two launched in March 2025.

Evidence for No:
- The menu was unchanged as of 2026-11-12.
- FURA has not signalled any new cultured protein, and the April 2026 Star feature mentions only quail.
- FURA did not pick up Parima chicken despite a year of availability.
- Aleph's launches have slipped before, and it has approvals but no production line.
- A new item would also have to appear on the menu itself, not just at a pop-up event.

(e) No scenario: Aleph production slips to late 2027, Parima launches with a handful of fine-dining restaurants other than FURA, and Volume Three keeps quail as its only cultured meat.

Yes scenario: Parima or Aleph chooses FURA as a launch partner because of its awards profile, and a duck parfait or beef snack appears in a spring 2027 menu refresh.

(f) I start at about 10%. I move up to about 15% because two new suppliers specifically target high-end Singapore restaurants within the window, FURA's profile is high and a menu refresh looks likely. I stay well below even odds because of the short window, the status quo, FURA's history of ignoring available chicken and the frequent delays in cultured meat launches.

Probability: 15%

(a) About 7.5 months remain (now 2026-11-12, deadline 2027-07-01). For Yes, FURA's menu must at some point list an item containing a cultured meat other than Japanese quail, such as Parima chicken or duck, Aleph beef, GOOD Meat chicken or cultivated seafood. The dish may later be removed.

(b) Status quo: No. The only cultured meat on the menu is Vow's Japanese quail, used in the parfait, the martini and the tallow.

(c) Base rate: FURA has served one cultured species for about 2.5 years. GOOD Meat chicken was approved throughout that time and Parima chicken from October 2025, and FURA added neither. Its rate of adding new species is close to zero per year. Broader context: approved cultivated products in Singapore rarely reach restaurant menus quickly, and restaurants that have adopted one tend to stick with one supplier. A reference rate of about 10% for a 7-month window seems reasonable.

(d) Evidence for Yes:
- More approved supply now exists: Parima duck (April 2026) aimed at "premium culinary channels", and Aleph beef (August 2026) planning a launch with select restaurant partners in the first half of 2027.
- FURA won World's Best Bar in July 2026, which makes it an attractive showcase partner.
- A Volume Three menu looks overdue, since Volume Two launched in March 2025.

Evidence for No:
- As of November 2026, the menu has no second species and no partnership has been announced.
- FURA has a deep, co-branded relationship with Vow ("Forged by FURA").
- Parima's foie-gras-style duck competes directly with Vow's Forged Gras.
- Aleph's timelines have slipped before, and its production only starts in the first half of 2027, which is tight.
- Both reports found no statements from FURA about new cultured proteins.

(e) No scenario: FURA launches Volume Three in early 2027, building on Vow quail and other future proteins such as insects and jellyfish. Aleph's line slips into late 2027 and Parima launches with fine-dining restaurants rather than a cocktail bar.

Yes scenario: Aleph or Parima picks the newly crowned World's Best Bar as a launch partner, and FURA adds a cultivated beef or duck snack to its menu in spring 2027.

(f) I start from a base rate of about 10% and move up to about 15%. The increase reflects the new approvals, Aleph's restaurant-first launch plan falling inside the window, FURA's higher profile and a menu refresh that seems due. I stay low because the status quo is strong, nothing has been announced, the Vow relationship looks exclusive in practice, and the window is short.

Probability: 14%

(a) There are about 7.5 months left (until 2027-07-01). For Yes, FURA's menu must list, at some point before then, an item containing a cultured meat other than Japanese quail, such as Parima/Gourmey chicken or duck, Aleph beef, GOOD Meat chicken, or a new Vow species. Forged Gras and Forged tallow are quail products, so they do not count.

(b) If nothing changes, the answer is No. As of 2026-11-12, quail is the only cultured meat on the menu.

(c) Base rate: FURA has run for about 3 years and has never added a second cultured species. That is despite GOOD Meat chicken being approved since 2020 and Parima chicken since October 2025. Restaurant rollouts of newly approved cultivated products in Singapore have been slow and limited. The rate of new-species additions works out to roughly 0 per 3 years. A naive base rate for a 7.5-month window is around 10%.

(d) Evidence:
- For Yes:
  - Aleph's cultivated beef was approved on 2026-08-04, with a planned H1 2027 launch "with select restaurant partners" and talks described as "active".
  - Parima duck was approved in April 2026, aimed at premium Singapore restaurants.
  - FURA was named World's Best Bar in July 2026, which makes it an attractive showcase partner, and its brand is built around future foods.
  - A Volume Three menu looks due, since Volume Two launched around March 2025.
- For No:
  - FURA has not adopted any other available cultured meat in 3 years. Chicken from two suppliers has been available.
  - Aleph has a history of slipping timelines, and its production line will not start until H1 2027, leaving little time before the deadline.
